subject: MSA / Order Form — IP carveouts, training restrictions, and next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@novadata.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novadata.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines — output ownership & training carveouts

Sean —

Thanks for sending the MSA and Order Form. Our legal team did an initial pass and attached a redline (nova_redline_MSA_20271009.pdf). Two high‑level asks from us: can Redwood confirm (1) that NovaData owns output (generated responses) when fed our proprietary prompts/data, and (2) that Redwood will not use our non‑public data to continue training or improve any models without explicit opt‑in (we need a clear training opt‑out).

We understand Redwood’s standard feedback/license clause, but we need a firm, contractual carveout for productization scenarios and an evidence pathway for audits. Our procurement team also needs a timeline for legal review so we can align internal signoff.

Can you loop in the appropriate contacts on your side and indicate where Redwood can accept carveouts vs. where you need a counterproposal?

Appreciate it —
Samantha Li
Legal Ops — NovaData Systems
Attachments: nova_redline_MSA_20271009.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@novadata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — output ownership & training carveouts

Samantha — thanks for the fast review and the redline. I circulated the PDF to Monica and our legal/product teams. Quick summary of our position so procurement can plan:

- Output ownership: Redwood’s baseline MSA provides customers a broad license to use outputs, but assignment/ownership requests are handled case‑by‑case. We can accept a limited, non‑exclusive ownership/assignment for outputs tied directly to customer data (e.g., prompts + proprietary DB) provided there are carveouts that preserve Redwood’s ability to operate, host, and maintain models.

- Training opt‑out: We support a contractable training opt‑out. Typical language is to prohibit use of non‑public customer content for model training, with an exception for aggregated telemetry needed for safety/compliance if mutually agreed. We will ask legal for proposed Exhibit A language.

- Evidence / audit path: We can provide attestations and a model of records (audit logs, config snapshots). Full forensic proof (e.g., raw KV cache dumps) is harder for operational security reasons — we can propose a staged evidence pathway (audit summary -> technical attestation -> on‑site evidence under NDA).

Action items: Monica / Laura, can you review Samantha’s redline and propose contract language for: (A) explicit training opt‑out sentence, (B) a productization carveout that avoids blocking Redwood ops, and (C) a practical audit/evidence workflow?

Samantha / NovaData procurement: please confirm target legal signoff date so I can align internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwoodinference.com

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — draft language and evidence workflow

Team — I reviewed NovaData’s PDF and drafted proposed language for Exhibit A (attached: proposed_exhibitA_training_limits.docx). Key points in my draft:

1) Training opt‑out clause (short): "Customer Content will not be used to train or improve any production or research models without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may use aggregated telemetry and anonymous usage metrics for service stability and security, subject to the exclusions below."

2) Productization carveout: narrow carveout that allows Redwood to (a) use transient caches for request routing and debugging, (b) store logs for operational troubleshooting for up to 90 days, and (c) preserve rights to improvements developed independently of Customer Content. Any use beyond this requires written consent.

3) Audit/evidence ladder: propose three tiers — (i) signed attestation from Redwood security team, (ii) time‑boxed access to sanitized logs under NDA, (iii) third‑party audit on a mutually acceptable scope and timetable. We avoid handing over production artifacts that risk other customers.

I recommend we propose the above as Redwood’s counter and offer a 2‑week window for legal redlines.

Monica
Legal & Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_exhibitA_training_limits.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — ML constraints and operational notes

Couple of technical clarifications to support the legal language:

- Definition of "Customer Content": we should be precise that this includes prompts, files, attachments, and any non‑public telemetry mapped to the account. This prevents ambiguity about what qualifies for opt‑out.

- "Use to train" needs scope: does NovaData want to block fine‑tuning, incremental online updates, and offline model re‑training? Recommend we enumerate: no fine‑tuning/further training using Customer Content; allowed uses: ephemeral caching, routing, and aggregated non‑attributable telemetry.

- Evidence: We can deliver configuration snapshots, model variant identifiers, tokenization metadata and sampling seeds used for a given timeframe. We cannot provide raw model weight diffs or internal training corpora. If the customer insists on deeper proof, we should offer a scoped third‑party attestation.

I’ll coordinate with infra to produce a sample audit kit so NovaData understands what we can provide. That will help negotiations.

— Karthik
Applied ML — Redwood Inference

Procurement would like to close the legal redline loop this month.

I'm attaching a DocuSign link (docusign_novadata_orderform_link.txt) for the updated Order Form with a training opt‑out checkbox and a placeholder clause for output assignment. We'll accept Redwood's proposed operational carveouts but ask you to confirm the 90‑day log retention limit in writing.

Next steps: Sean — can you confirm internal signoff (ops + legal) and provide the draft Exhibit A document back to us by EOD Wednesday (2027‑10‑13)? If we have those, procurement will route for final approval.

Samantha Li
